items.why: The report finds the high-side extra band ("a narrow band at ~358 cm-1 is present at 4 K ... and 80 K") but does not report a low-frequency shoulder near 220 cm-1 on the ~240 mode; it reports a ~300 cm-1 band instead.

It says the 358 band is strongest at 4 K (height 65), weaker at 80 K (height 17) and "not significant at 150 K ... or 300 K", that it "brackets the bulk T_N (~132 K)", and calls this "suggestive of magnetic-order-related effects".
It assigns no symmetry and says "no mode symmetry can be assigned from these spectra".

Both the ~240 and ~341 modes soften as temperature rises (341.32→338.38 and 242.11→237.02 cm-1), and the 341 mode broadens to 6.85 cm-1 at 300 K, which is the same physics; the report does not note that Ag2 broadens more.

It says the 341 shifts are "consistent with ordinary anharmonic behaviour", that it cannot separate the trends from "ordinary anharmonicity", and that "the changes that matter are in the weaker bands", meaning the band that appears at low temperature.

It notes that crossed circular detection "selects a subset of modes that depends on the symmetry and convention", but it does not say intensities change between parallel/crossed or σ+/σ− settings, or that comparisons need one fixed configuration.
It asks for "a dense sweep (about 10 K steps between 100 and 160 K)" and for "a reference spectrum of bulk or few-layer CrSBr taken with the same setup".

wrong_claims.why: It states the 358 band is "not significant at 150 K ... or 300 K" and reports no 220 feature; the ~300 cm-1 band it places at 150 K is a different feature.
It says the modes harden on cooling, i.e. they soften with increasing temperature (338.38 at 300 K to 341.41 cm-1 at 4 K).

items.why: The report says B at 4 K has a low-frequency doublet component, "about 246.1 and 250.3 cm-1", and "a mode at 361.1 cm-1 that is absent from A at 4 K and from both 300 K spectra", while A's band is "a single line". This is the same physics, with peak positions close to the rubric's.
The report explicitly declines to assign thickness: "which flake is thicker is undetermined" and "no thickness is assigned to either flake".

The report only tentatively links the features to magnetism. It suggests spin-phonon coupling "below the magnetic transitions (T_N ~132 K)" for the cooling shift and asks whether "the B-only doublet and 361 cm-1 mode turn on at T_N", but it attributes B's extra features mainly to possible inhomogeneity.

The report records B's modes as slightly lower ("300 K centres differ by 0.5 and 1.2 cm-1"), but it gives this for 300 K rather than 4 K and does not link it to the redshift with decreasing layer number.
The report states: "Both flakes shift to higher wavenumber on cooling: the high mode by +3.6 (A) and +3.5 (B) cm-1, the low mode by +8.2 (A) ... and +4.9 (B)".
The report states: "Absolute intensities ... are therefore not meaningful". It cites the processing mismatch and interference on SiO2/Si, and declines to judge thickness from intensity.
The report asks "What are the AFM thicknesses (pending)" and requests "A temperature series between 4 K and 150 K (across T_N ~132 K)".

wrong_claims.why: The report states that the extra 4 K features appear in B and are absent from A.
The report leaves thickness undetermined and never calls A the thinner flake.

items.why: It fits all three modes (P1 ~104–114, P2 ~238–244, P4 ~340–343 cm-1) and says "The 341 cm-1 (P4) mode is the strongest feature in all six flakes", with P1/P4 and P2/P4 area ratios well below 1, but it leaves them "unassigned" rather than identifying them as Ag modes.

It reports that B, D and F sit higher than C and E in P1/P2, but it never links the higher frequency to more layers; it only lists thickness as one possible cause ("consistent with strain, thickness, orientation or local heating").
It notes P4 shifts less than P1/P2, but it never says Ag3 is a poor layer-number indicator, and it actually builds its ranking on the 341 cm-1 mode.
Its tentative ranking "D > F > A > B > E > C" puts bulk-like flake B in the middle, so it does not match the expected order B > D ≥ F > A > E > C.
It assigns no layer numbers ("no thickness value is given for any flake") and does not identify C as a monolayer or B as bulk.

It says intensity is "confounded by orientation" ("CrSBr is strongly anisotropic") and that mode ratios "are orientation-dependent... should not be read as thickness indicators without polarization data".
It asks for AFM ("Please share AFM thickness for the six flakes") and asks whether the polarization and in-plane angle were controlled.

wrong_claims.why: It ranks the flakes by Ag3 intensity relative to background, not by Ag3 position, so this claim as worded is not made (although that intensity proxy is also unreliable).
It never says Ag1/Ag2 soften as flakes get thicker.

items.why: The report fits "A1' (~240-241 cm-1)" in every spectrum and calls it "the dominant feature", which identifies it as the main first-order peak.

The report lists the ~481, ~531 and ~583 cm-1 bands only as "Weaker bands". It never says they are the strongest features after the one-phonon peak, that they are absent at the 1.65 eV A1s resonance, or that they are specific to the 2s resonance.

The report places the resonance near 2.04 eV at "a higher-lying optical transition (B-exciton region or above)" but gives the B exciton as 1.8-1.95 eV. It never identifies the B2s exciton near 2.016 eV or any incoming/outgoing resonance structure.

It tentatively assigns the peaks to Gamma-phonon combinations ("~481 is consistent with 2A1'... ~531 with A1'+E'... ~583 with 2E'"). It does not interpret them as intravalley scattering between Rydberg exciton states, and it suggests 531 may be an instrumental ghost.

It places the 1.65 eV spectra at "the neutral/charged A-exciton region" and notes a "~100x intensity" difference between the groups. However, it attributes the difference to possible normalization problems ("cannot be attributed to physics until normalization is verified") rather than to a real drop in scattering at the 2s resonance.

It warns that "Subtracting crossed from parallel can remove part of the in-plane E' signal". It also flags negative counts and asks whether the broad hump is residual PL left by the parallel/crossed subtraction.

It says the assignments of the weaker bands "are tentative" and gives alternatives for 531 cm-1. It never states that only the A1' peak has a firm single-phonon assignment, and it treats E' as firmly assigned.
It asks for "PL, reflectance contrast or PLE measured on this same spot" to "pin the neutral exciton, trion and B-exciton energies and tell us what the 2.04 eV resonance is".

wrong_claims.why: It only hedges that the 531 cm-1 line "may be instrumental" or a "substrate/spectrometer artifact" and lists A1'+E' as an option. It does not assign the three peaks to Si or hBN.
It never claims the 480/531/583 cm-1 peaks are present at the 1.65 eV resonance; for 1.6791 eV it reports peaks at 240, 289, 303 and 320 cm-1 only.

items.why: The report notes that "the 350 cm⁻¹ component overlaps E′" and tries a "two-component E′ fit". It also mentions separating "E′ from 2LA(M)-type contributions". However, it never assigns the ~351 component firmly to 2LA(M), calls it "ambiguous", and gives no stable fit.
The report gives no 2LA(M)/A1g intensity ratio and makes no spot-1 vs spot-2 comparison. It says "E′ and 2LA-type intensities are not quantified here."
Only a single A1g position (~418 cm⁻¹) is reported for one flake. There are no 417.2 vs 420.1 cm⁻¹ values for two spots and no monolayer-vs-bulk contrast.
The report gives one separation, "60.75 ± 0.24 cm⁻¹", not ~62 and ~65 cm⁻¹ for the two spots. It does not compute the separation after a stable E′/2LA(M) split.
The report says the separation "is consistent with a monolayer or few-layer flake but does not fix the layer number". It does not give the ~1 cm⁻¹ step size between 2L, 3L and bulk.
The report checks calibration against Si: "Si 520.7 cm⁻¹ reference fits to 521.6 ± 0.5 cm⁻¹". It also discusses excitation-dependent resonance at length.

wrong_claims.why: The report does build layer number on the A1g−E′ separation, with E′ at ~357 cm⁻¹. However, it explicitly fits a separate ~350 component rather than assigning the band maximum to E′ alone.
The ~350 band is never called a defect or impurity peak. The report says there is "no clear defect-activated D-like band".

items.why: The report gives a large drop on warming at the higher laser energies ("falls by about 2 decades from 4 K to 295 K at 587 nm and about 1.5 decades at 599 nm") and its areas imply a peak intensity about 10x higher at 4 K (1.09e6 vs 1.1e5). But it frames the change as depending on which side of the resonance you are on, with intensity rising at 623 nm, and never states an overall order-of-magnitude increase on cooling.

It states "The resonance maximum moves from at least 2.11 eV (4 K) to about 2.05 eV (150 K) to about 2.01 eV (295 K)" and ties this to the A-exciton "red-shift of about 0.1 eV from 4 K to 295 K... consistent with the measured resonance movement".
No low-temperature structure (exciton/trion channels, incoming/outgoing resonances) is identified; the report calls the 4 K profile "monotonic with a maximum at the highest laser energy".
Trions and separate exciton/trion resonance amplitudes are never mentioned.

It shows that a fixed-wavelength comparison gives opposite trends "on either side of the resonance", names the exciton resonance as "the dominant effect" on intensities, and notes that four energies "sample the resonance coarsely".
Thin-film interference on SiO2/Si and the need for reflectivity correction are not mentioned; only the cryostat window, focus and Si throughput variation are raised.
It asks: "Was a power series at 4 K... or a Stokes/anti-Stokes measurement made to estimate the laser-heated local temperature?"

wrong_claims.why: The Bose-Einstein factor is never invoked; the intensity change is put down to the exciton resonance.
The report says the maximum moves to lower energy on warming, which means higher energy on cooling (the correct direction).

items.why: The report says the "~249 cm-1 first-order band peaks at 1.870 eV and again at 1.900 eV" and explains this as the "incoming and outgoing resonances" of a state it calls a 2s candidate.
It gives "candidate_2s_exciton_eV: 1.870 (about 130 meV above A1s at 1.740 eV)".

Its integrals show the 495 band at 62.8 at 1.8703 eV, 4.9 at 1.8847 eV, then rising again, but the report never reads this as a single peak at the incoming resonance that vanishes and reappears about 26 meV higher; it treats 1.9325 eV as the main resonance.

The report contradicts dispersion ("sits at a fixed Raman shift across the whole series"); it notes the band is "not a single Lorentzian", but two-component fits were unstable and it never finds three peaks.
There is no claim that dark excitonic states are involved; the report explains the band as a two-phonon overtone with a "doubly outgoing resonance" of one state.

It calls the negative lobes "slight baseline over-subtraction" (a processing artifact) and notes that parallel-minus-crossed data limits symmetry assignment, but it never says depolarized signal and luminescence are removed, and it even raises a possible "photoluminescence pedestal".
It says the identity is "Not established: 2E' vs 2A1' vs a combination", but still calls it "most likely two-phonon overtone", so it does not treat the assignment as fully open.

wrong_claims.why: It calls the band the "~495 cm-1 two-phonon overtone" that "sits at a fixed Raman shift across the whole series", which denies the dispersion.
It rejects substrate origin: the resonance "is not explained by SiO2 or the Si reference", and the pedestal "is not a fixed substrate background".

items.why: The report lists an extra band at "358.3" (4 K) and "357.6" (80 K) on the high side of Ag3 but never mentions a ~220 cm-1 shoulder or Ag2 asymmetry, and it does not call either feature a new low-temperature feature.

The band lists show the ~358 cm-1 band at 4 K and 80 K and missing at 150 K and 300 K, but the report does not say it is weaker at 80 K and makes no link to the Néel temperature, magnetic order or spin-phonon coupling.
The report assigns no symmetry to any band; the 358 cm-1 band is only listed as "bands at ... 358.3" and is never called B3g.

The fitted positions show both main bands moving up on cooling (237.0→242.0 and 338.4→341.4; "strongest band of 4 K shifts by -2.99 cm-1 in 300 K"), but the report never states the narrowing trend or that Ag2 broadens more than Ag3.
The caveats list is empty, and the report never mentions anharmonic or multiphonon effects as an alternative explanation.
The report says nothing about intensities depending on the circular polarization configuration.
"questions_for_user" is empty, so the report asks neither for finer temperature steps nor for a bulk reference.

wrong_claims.why: The 150 K and 300 K band lists ("240.1, 300.8, 340.6" and "237.0, 338.4") contain no band near 220 or 355 cm-1.
The report gives higher frequencies at low temperature (338.4 at 300 K vs 341.4 at 4 K), which is hardening on cooling, not softening.

items.why: The report lists extra bands only for flake B at 4 K ("bands at 247.3, 342.6, 358.9, 361.0") and only two bands for A at 4 K and both 300 K spectra, but it never calls them low-temperature extra features, never reports the ~220 cm-1 Ag2 shoulder, and never compares the flakes on this point.
Nothing in the report concludes which flake is few-layer and which is bulk-like.
The report never mentions magnetic ordering, TN or spin-phonon coupling.
It gives the numbers ("strongest band of flake A, 4 K shifts by -1.31 cm-1 in flake B, 4 K"; 250.0 vs 247.3 cm-1), but it does not identify the modes as Ag2/Ag3 or link the redshift to layer number.

The fitted positions show both bands higher at 4 K than at 300 K in both flakes, and it states a -3.63 cm-1 shift for flake A, but there is no explicit statement that both modes harden on cooling in both flakes.
The caveats list is empty, and nothing is said about intensities, baselines or the different export processing.
The questions_for_user list is empty, so there is no request for AFM thickness or intermediate temperatures.

wrong_claims.why: The report lists only two bands for flake A at 4 K and never attributes extra modes to flake A.
The report makes no claim about which flake is thinner.

items.why: The report lists fitted band positions such as "108.33", "241.34" and "341.11" cm-1, but it never assigns them as Ag1/Ag2/Ag3 modes or says that Ag1 and Ag2 are weaker than Ag3.
The report never links the Ag1/Ag2 positions to thickness; it only gives raw fits per flake.
No caveat appears ("caveats": []), and nothing is said about Ag3 being insensitive to thickness.
There is no thickness ranking; the only comparison is "strongest band of flake A shifts by ..." relative to flake A.
No flake is called a monolayer or bulk; flakes C and B appear only as lists of bands.
Polarization or orientation dependence of intensities is never mentioned; the caveats and limits lists are empty.
"questions_for_user": [] is empty; there is no request for AFM or polarization/orientation information.

wrong_claims.why: The report gives shifts of the strongest (~341 cm-1, Ag3) band relative to flake A, but it never uses them to draw any thickness conclusion.
The report makes no statement about which way Ag1/Ag2 shift with thickness.

items.why: The report lists a band near 241 cm-1 in every spectrum (e.g. "241.30+-0.03 cm-1, FWHM 2.0") and tracks the "strongest band", but it never assigns it to A1'(Γ) or calls it the one-phonon peak.

Bands near 480.7, 531 and 582 cm-1 appear in the fitted lists, but the report never says they are the strongest features after the one-phonon peak, that they are missing at the 1.65 eV spectra, or that they are tied to the 2s resonances.
The report does not mention the B2s exciton or any incoming or outgoing resonance.
The report gives no assignment to Γ-phonon combinations (2E', A1'+E', 2A1') and does not mention intravalley Rydberg scattering.
The report does not place the low-energy spectra at the A1s exciton and does not compare absolute scattering intensities.
The caveats list is empty, and the report says nothing about parallel-minus-crossed subtraction artifacts.
The report has no caveat about weak peaks having uncertain multiphonon or defect assignments; it makes no assignments at all.
The questions list is empty; the report does not suggest finer excitation steps or reflectivity on the same spot.

wrong_claims.why: The report makes no assignments, so it never attributes the peaks to Si or hBN.
The report does not claim these peaks are equally present at the A1s resonance; the 1.65 eV fits list different bands.

items.why: The report finds the high-side peak ("A ~358 cm-1 band (17 cm-1 blue of Ag3) is present at 4 K ... and 80 K"), but the Ag2 shoulder it notes is "near 248 cm-1" at 80 K, on the high side, not a low-side shoulder near 220 cm-1.

It gets the temperature pattern right ("present at 4 and 80 K; absent at 150 and 300 K", 80 K height 18.6 vs 64.7 at 4 K, "appears below the bulk T_N (~132–134 K)") but only calls it a "magnetic candidate" and never commits to magnetic order or spin-phonon coupling.
It says "Neither is assigned" and never names a B3g mode for the ~358 cm-1 band.

Hardening on cooling is clear ("Ag2 ... +5.0 ± 0.3 cm-1 and Ag3 ... +3.0 ± 0.2 cm-1"), but narrowing is shown only partly ("The 300 K value is the broadest" for Ag3); Ag2 widths are non-monotonic, and the report does not show Ag2 broadening more than Ag3.

It calls the softening with rising T "the usual anharmonic pattern", says "Four temperatures cannot show a spin-phonon anomaly", and treats the band that "switches off between 80 and 150 K" as the magnetic candidate.

It notes that "crossed-circular is also the helicity-reversing channel where magnetic antisymmetric-tensor terms ... appear" and asks for co-circular spectra, but never says intensities depend on configuration or that comparisons need one fixed configuration.

It notes "Four temperatures cannot resolve the flat-then-jump behaviour ... near 25 K" and that "No transition temperature is bracketed beyond 80 K < T_x < 150 K", but asks for power and field series rather than finer temperature steps or a bulk reference.

wrong_claims.why: It says the 358 band is "absent at 150 K and 300 K"; the band it reports at 150 K is at ~300 cm-1, not 220 or 355 cm-1.
It states that both modes "harden" on cooling from 300 K.

items.why: The report finds extra structure only in flake B at 4 K: a non-single-line Ag2 with a low-frequency component at 246.2 cm-1 and an "extra band in flake B at 4 K only, at 361 cm-1", which is absent in flake A at 4 K and in B at 300 K. The positions differ from the rubric's (no shoulder near 220 cm-1, and the band is at 361 rather than ~355), so this gets half credit.
The report says layers are "not determined" and reads flake B as "a spot that sees more than one region... or a more disordered region", so it never concludes that B is few-layer and A is bulk-like.
The report states "The 361 cm-1 band is not assignable" and rejects the magnetic IR-mode candidate, so it does not link the extra features to magnetic order or spin-phonon coupling.

The report notes that B is lower at 4 K ("Ag2 is ... -2.7 cm-1 at 4 K", "Ag3 is -1.3 cm-1") but argues the temperature dependence "argues against a simple thickness offset", so it does not frame the shift as the layer-number redshift.
The report gives "Ag2 shifts +8.23 cm-1 (A) and +5.98 cm-1 (B)... Ag3 shifts +3.63 (A) and +3.54 (B)" from 300 K to 4 K, i.e. both modes harden on cooling in both flakes.

The report states "absolute intensities and intensity ratios are not comparable between flakes" because of the different export processing, and also mentions thin-film interference and unknown thickness.
The report asks "What are the flake thicknesses (AFM or optical contrast)..." and also says a temperature series is needed for any magnetic claim.

wrong_claims.why: The report says flake A has "no extra bands in the window" and puts the extra features in B.
The report leaves layer number undetermined and never says flake A is thinner.

items.why: The report names the triplet "near 108–114 (Ag1), 238–244 (Ag2) and 340–343 cm-1 (Ag3)" and gives fitted positions, but it never says that Ag1 and Ag2 are much weaker than Ag3; it only lists Ag3 counts.
It states "Ag1 redshifts as layer number decreases" and "Ag1 and Ag2 redshift as layers are removed", and it treats the flake with the lowest Ag1 (A) as the thinnest, so higher Ag1 means thicker.
It says "Ag3 is nearly layer-independent in the literature" and "Ag3 flat", and it puts the Ag3 scatter down to calibration or strain rather than thickness.
The order "A < F ≈ D ≈ B" matches part of the correct sequence (by Ag1, A<F<D<B), but C and E are left unplaced ("C and E cannot be placed") when they are the two thinnest flakes.
C is not identified as a monolayer (it is "not placed"), and B is matched to "the 4-layer reference" instead of being called bulk-like.

It says that with unknown polarization, "if C and E sit with b perpendicular to the laser polarization, Ag1 and Ag3 would be suppressed without any thickness change", and that counts "do not map to thickness".
It asks for "AFM heights for flakes A to F" and for "the laser polarization relative to the flake's long edge ... and the orientation of each flake" to confirm the ranking.

wrong_claims.why: The ranking uses Ag1 position and the Ag1−Ag3 separation, and the report explicitly treats Ag3 as thickness-independent.
It says Ag1 and Ag2 redshift as layers are removed, which means they stiffen with thickness, the correct direction.

items.why: The report identifies the peak directly: "A1' ... is the dominant first-order line across the whole series and sits at 241 to 242 cm-1 after calibration."
The report lists bands at 480–503, 531 and 582–586 cm-1, but treats them as substrate, background or unassigned, and never says they are missing at 1.65 eV or tied to 2s resonances.
The high-energy resonance is called "an E'-favouring resonance near 2.00 to 2.05 eV that I cannot assign"; the report never mentions B2s or incoming/outgoing resonances.
The 480/531/583 peaks are never assigned to combinations of Gamma-point phonons or to intravalley Rydberg-exciton scattering.

The report assumes "the A exciton (and trion) is near 1.64 to 1.68 eV" and finds A1' "about 22 to 27 times larger" there, which is a large drop but not roughly two orders of magnitude, and it doubts the absolute scale.

It notes that "Parallel minus crossed subtraction does not remove all luminescence or depolarised substrate light," which covers residual background, but it does not say depolarized Raman features are removed.
It warns that weak bands are "not reliable" and broad features are "fit-dependent," but treats both A1' and E' as firm and does not discuss multiple possible multi-phonon assignments.
It asks "Do you have PL or reflectance on this same flake at 4 K?" so the resonances can be assigned, and notes that "the 0.03 to 0.05 eV steps are too coarse to resolve a narrow resonance."

wrong_claims.why: The summary says the 430–600 cm-1 features are "partly background or substrate" and attributes 480–586 cm-1 to amorphous-SiO2 bands; this is labelled a hypothesis, but it is still the report's main attribution.
The report never claims these peaks are equally present at the 1.65 eV spectra.

items.why: The report fits the band with two components, "352.73 ± 0.32 (FWHM 10.17) and 358.46 ± 0.05," and assigns them to 2LA(M) and E2g1, but the E2g1 position (358.5 cm-1) is well off the about 355.2 cm-1 expected, and the spectra are not the two 514.5 nm spots in the case.
No 2LA(M)/A1g intensity ratio is given for either spot, and no monolayer fingerprint ratio is mentioned.
The report says A1g is "about 417.9 to 418.0 cm-1 in both spectra" and gives no stiffening from about 417.2 to 420.1 cm-1 between a thin and a thick spot.
No A1g minus E2g1 separation is reported for either spot.
Nothing is said about how weakly positions constrain 2L, 3L and bulk; layers are simply "not determined".
The report checks Si-line calibration ("Si offsets +1.355 and +0.298 cm-1"; "Was the spectrometer recalibrated between wavelengths?") and ties 2LA(M) visibility to excitation resonance.

wrong_claims.why: The report separates 2LA(M) and E2g1 into two components and builds no layer number on the band maximum.
2LA(M) is named as such; it is not called a defect or impurity peak.

items.why: The report only implies this through SNR, noting that "Signal-to-noise differs by roughly an order of magnitude between temperatures" (4K 587.7 nm 1106.9 vs 295K 54.6). It treats this as a data-quality issue and never states that the A1' Raman intensity rises on cooling.
The report never says the resonance maximum shifts with temperature or follows the exciton energy. It states "the A-exciton energy at 4, 150 and 295 K" was "not verified".
The report does not describe exciton/trion or incoming/outgoing structure at low temperature versus a single broad peak at room temperature.
The report does not discuss trion versus exciton contributions or their temperature dependence.

The report warns that "Intensity trends at fixed nominal wavelength mix temperature and resonance". However, it attributes this mainly to laser energies not matching across temperatures, and it does not say that a full excitation profile is needed at each temperature.
The report never mentions thin-film interference on 290 nm SiO2/Si or its temperature dependence.
The report asks "how was the sample temperature measured? Laser heating at 0.7 mW on a supported flake can shift the local temperature by an unknown amount."

wrong_claims.why: The report does not attribute any intensity change to the Bose-Einstein factor.
The report makes no claim about which direction the resonance shifts.

items.why: The report puts the 248-250 cm-1 maximum at 1.8703 eV and lists a second high area (244 at 1.8999 eV), but it never names a double incoming/outgoing resonance or the A2s exciton; the summary says only that the peak 'falls by more than 30x by 1.94 eV'.
It gives the resonance at '1.8703 eV (+130 meV above A1s)' but does not assign it to the A2s, saying only that PLE 'would turn the 1.870 eV ... resonances into exciton assignments'.
The report says the 480-510 group is 'present in 8 of 9 spectra' and does not describe it appearing only at the A2s incoming resonance, vanishing just above it, then reappearing about 26 meV higher.
It reports strong growth near 1.93 eV and resolves a doublet at 492.7/495.9 cm-1, but it finds two peaks, not three, and explicitly denies dispersion: 'not as a dispersive or strain-like shift'.
The report rejects dispersion and does not infer dark excitonic states with minima or saddle points in their dispersion.
It notes the parallel-minus-crossed subtraction 'removes most of the E' intensity', but it does not say that residual background or negative values are processing artifacts.
It states 'The 495 group has no assignment in the notes I read' and that the overtone or combination ideas 'are arithmetic hypotheses, not verified'.

wrong_claims.why: It denies dispersion, but it does not assert the feature is a 2A1' overtone; it lists '2 x 248 = 496' only as an unverified hypothesis.
It does not attribute the 495 cm-1 feature to Si or hBN; Si is discussed only for the 520 cm-1 calibration line.
